/-!
# Erdős Problem 409

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/409](https://www.erdosproblems.com/409)
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped Topology ArithmeticFunction.sigma Nat
open Filter

namespace Erdos409

/--
How many iterations of $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$ are needed before a prime is reached?
-/
-- Formalisation note: the sequence of iterates always terminates if `n > 0`
-- since it is strictly decreasing unless the input is prime, at which point
-- it becomes static. See also https://oeis.org/A39651
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.parts.i (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    IsLeast { i | (φ · + 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/-- If $n > 0$, then the iteration $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$ necessarily
reaches a prime. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.variants.termination (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    ∃ i, (φ · + 1)^[i] n |>.Prime := by
  induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | _ n ih =>
    by_cases hp : n.Prime
    · exact ⟨0, by simpa using hp⟩
    · have h1 : n = 1 ∨ 1 < n := by omega
      rcases h1 with h1 | h1
      · subst h1
        refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
        norm_num [Function.iterate_one, Nat.totient_one]
      · have hlt : φ n < n := Nat.totient_lt n h1
        have hne : φ n ≠ n - 1 := by
          intro h
          exact hp ((Nat.totient_eq_iff_prime hn).1 h)
        have hdec : φ n + 1 < n := by omega
        have hpos : 0 < φ n + 1 := by positivity
        obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := ih (φ n + 1) hdec hpos
        refine ⟨i + 1, ?_⟩
        rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply]
        exact hi

-- Formalisation note: it's possible that solution to `erdos_409.parts.i` needs to be
-- expressed asymptotically. To handle this we include `IsTheta`, `IsBigO`
-- and `IsLittleO` variants below. Since a solution is not known this necessitates
-- the use of an `answer(sorry)` placeholder. Trivial or sub-optimal solutions
-- will therefore exist to the asymptotic formalisations. A true solution to
-- the asymptotic variants should have a degree of optimality or non-triviality to it.
/--
Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$ before a prime
is reached. What is $\Theta(c(n))$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.parts.i.isTheta (c : ℕ → ℕ)
    (h : ∀ n > 0, IsLeast { i | (φ · + 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } (c n)) :
    (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$ before a prime
is reached. Find the simplest function $g(n)$ such that $c(n) = O(g(n))$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.parts.i.isBigO (c : ℕ → ℕ)
    (h : ∀ n > 0, IsLeast { i | (φ · + 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } (c n)) :
    (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$ before a prime
is reached. Find the simplest function $g(n)$ such that $c(n) = o(g(n))$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.parts.i.isLittleO (c : ℕ → ℕ)
    (h : ∀ n > 0, IsLeast { i | (φ · + 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } (c n)) :
    (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Can infinitely many $n$ reach the same prime under the iteration $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.parts.ii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime), { n | ∃ i, (φ · + 1)^[i] n = p }.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
What is the density of $n$ which reach any fixed prime under the iteration $n\mapsto\phi(n) + 1$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.parts.iii (p : ℕ) (h : p.Prime) :
    { n | ∃ i, (φ · + 1)^[i] n = p }.HasDensity answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/--
If the iteration $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ starting at $n > 1$ reaches a prime, how many
iterations are needed before a prime is reached?
-/
-- Formalisation note: termination of this sequence is not known in general since
-- it is strictly increasing except at primes, so it is assumed as a hypothesis.
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.variants.sigma (n : ℕ) (hn : n > 1)
    (hterm : ∃ i, (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime) :
    IsLeast { i | (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/-- If $n > 1$ then the iteration $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ necessarily reaches a prime.
Note: this is open — it is not clear that the σ iteration always terminates,
since it is non-decreasing (unlike the φ iteration which is strictly decreasing). -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.variants.sigma_termination (n : ℕ) (hn : n > 1) :
    ∃ i, (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime := by
  sorry

-- Formalisation note: See the above formalisation note for the rationale
-- for including asymptotic variants
/--
Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ before a prime
is reached. What is $\Theta(c(n))$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.variants.sigma_isTheta (c : ℕ → ℕ)
    (h : ∀ n > 1, IsLeast { i | (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } (c n)) :
    (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ before a prime
is reached. Find the simplest function $g(n)$ such that $c(n) = O(g(n))$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.variants.sigma_isBigO (c : ℕ → ℕ)
    (h : ∀ n > 1, IsLeast { i | (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } (c n)) :
    (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Let $c(n)$ be the minimum number of iterations of $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ before a prime
is reached. Find the simplest function $g(n)$ such that $c(n) = o(g(n))$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.variants.sigma_isLittleO (c : ℕ → ℕ)
    (h : ∀ n > 1, IsLeast { i | (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime } (c n)) :
    (fun n => (c n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
Is it true that iterates of $n\mapsto\sigma(n) - 1$ always reach a prime?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_409.variants.sigma_prime_termination :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n > 1, ∃ i, (σ 1 · - 1)^[i] n |>.Prime := by
  sorry

end Erdos409

findings.description: The formalisation note immediately above this theorem says that the iteration is strictly decreasing unless its input is prime, under the stated condition n > 0. This overlooks n = 1: 1 is not prime, but φ(1) + 1 = 2 > 1. Only the explanation is wrong; the termination theorem is correct, and its proof explicitly handles this exception.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A039650, N. J. A. Sloane's comment of September 22, 2017, explicitly restricts the decreasing-trajectory argument to n > 1. OEIS A039649 starts with f(1) = 2, and A039651 records one iteration from 1. These entries were read in the official OEIS data files. The counterexample was also verified in /workspace/review/boundaries.lean.
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify the note: for n > 1, a nonprime input strictly decreases and a prime is fixed; the remaining positive input 1 maps directly to the prime 2. No theorem statement needs changing.

reformulations.difference: The basin is a set of all natural-number starting values, including 0, rather than only positive starting values.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Restricting the basin to positive naturals removes at most the single element 0. Removing a finite set preserves infinitude, for each fixed prime and hence also under the existential quantifier over primes. The generic equivalence was proved in density-tests.lean.

reformulations.difference: The density is taken for the basin over ℕ, including the extra starting value 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Adding or removing 0 changes the count below N by at most one, so the normalized counts differ by at most 1/N for N > 0. Consequently existence and value of natural density are unchanged. The use of a strict upper endpoint in HasDensity likewise does not change natural density.

review.notes: Checked all thirteen declarations. No theorem-level misformalization or status mismatch was found. Small stopping times agree with the OEIS tables. Lean checks established prime fixed points, the boundary exceptions, satisfiability of the totient c-hypothesis, and equivalence of the sigma c-hypothesis's satisfiability with global termination. The sigma asymptotic statements are therefore appropriately conditional. Trivial or coarse fillings of the asymptotic answer slots are not findings under CONTRIBUTING.md. Direct Erdős/OEIS HTML access was blocked; the Erdős reader omitted mathematical displays, so functions and indexing were cross-checked against official OEIS data and the linked literature.
